summary.text: Mary Gay Scanlon is the Democratic incumbent, in the U.S. House since a November 2018 special election. A lawyer who worked in legal-aid and child-advocacy roles and later directed pro bono programs at a national law firm, she also served as president of her local school board. She serves on the Judiciary and Rules committees.

paragraphs.text: Born in Syracuse, New York, in 1959.
Earned a bachelor's degree in history from Colgate University (1980) and a J.D. from the University of Pennsylvania Law School (1984).
Worked as a law clerk and as an attorney at Ballard Spahr, the Education Law Center of Pennsylvania and the Support Center for Child Advocates.

Her official biography says she was national pro bono counsel at a major U.S. law firm, where she directed and supervised over 600 lawyers in 15 offices providing more than 50,000 hours of pro bono legal services annually.
Before Congress, served as president of her local school board and co-chair of the Voting Rights Task Force of the Association of Pro Bono Counsel.
Sworn into the U.S. House on November 13, 2018, following a special election, and represents Pennsylvania's 5th District.

Serves on the House Committee on Rules and the Judiciary Committee, where she is ranking member of the Constitution and Limited Government Subcommittee; also chairs the House Caucuses on Access to Legal Aid, Youth Mentoring, and Foster Youth.

In the 119th Congress (2025-2026), Ballotpedia lists her Judiciary subcommittees as Immigration Integrity, Security, and Enforcement and The Constitution and Limited Government, and the Rules Subcommittee on Rules and Organization of the House.
Lives in Swarthmore with her husband, Mark; they have three adult children, according to her official biography.
